newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm ministers agree plant disease penalties.
newsitem.headline: Farm ministers agree plant disease penalties.

text.p: European Union farm ministers decided on Monday that national governments exporting plants and vegetables will face tough new penalties if they allow the export of plant and vegetable diseases, EU officials said.

"This is potentially a significant measure because governments will face the cost of eradicating any disease which they are found to have allowed across their frontier," Commission spokesman Gerard Kiely said.
Germany opposed the change to the directive on the prevention of harmful vegetable organisms (Directive 77/93) saying that the European Union already has penalties for non-compliance with EU law.
"The German position was that there should not be a need for additional legislation," a German diplomat said after Monday's decision.

Under the new rules, the EU will make a contribution to member states to help eradicate disease but a state found to have allowed the export of a disease will be required to repay the EU financial aid.
The agreement, which follows a European Parliament debate, allows the EU to provide additional finance for strengthening external border controls on plants and vegetables.
